source: OpenAlex works API: title_and_abstract.search counts, group_by=language, a fixed-seed sample (sample and seed), and an ids.openalex overlap check against the main query
method: Each term set is one OR-group of the strings registered for it in the project's search vocabulary register (the native-language probe rows only). For each set the probe asks OpenAlex for: the number of works whose title or abstract matches the group (count); how those works are labelled by language (language_label_counts, one request per set, skipped when the budget guard would refuse it); and a random sample of up to 50 works, drawn with the fixed seed 20261122 (sample). Each sampled work is then checked against the main plastics query, plastic-v3.1 with its type exclusions, to show which sampled works the main query also retrieves (sample_in_v31). That is an overlap on the sample only: a share of the sample, not a completeness rate for either query. Every request goes through the project's OpenAlex client and budget guard, and no paid filters are used. Cost is OpenAlex's reported credits at USD 0.0001 per credit, using for each request the larger of the reported cost and the credit price. Responses are cached, so the file can be rebuilt without network access.

caveats: Many non-English papers have English titles and abstracts. A match on a native-language term shows that the string appears in OpenAlex's indexed title or abstract. It does not show the paper's own language, and sample titles are OpenAlex metadata, which can be translated.

OpenAlex language labels are imperfect. The project's planning notes cite Céspedes et al. 2025 for false positives among declared-language labels. That source has not been checked against its text, so no error rate is claimed here. The counts use OpenAlex's labels as given.

Native-language hits include public-communication items, which are written for the public rather than as research articles. The term counts do not exclude document types; the overlap check applies the project's type exclusions.

OpenAlex's search matches stemmed word forms. The project's query notes record this for English terms (for example, 'microplasticity' matches 'microplastic'). The native-language strings were not tested for it, so a count may include related forms.

Some strings are spelled the same in other languages, so a set can contain works in other languages. For example, OpenAlex's labels for the German Mikroplastik set include Indonesian and Turkish works, which use the same word. The counts are not restricted to the labelled language; language_label_counts shows the split.
The 纳米塑料 set has mixed senses. The vocabulary register notes a 2001 materials article among its hits, so the count includes works outside plastic pollution research.

microplásticos is one set for Spanish and Portuguese, and the Norwegian and Danish strings are one set. OpenAlex counts are not split by language there. The register labels these strings Spanish or Norwegian only; no Portuguese or Danish strings are registered.

Counts are OpenAlex totals taken on the run date, under the search form described in the method. The A3 probe counts (2026-11-18) are shown for comparison. Most sets agree with them within about 7 per cent. The Chinese, Russian and Norwegian and Danish sets differ by much more, and index growth does not explain that. This probe does not confirm the search form behind the A3 figures, so compare the counts with them with care.

Each sample is a fixed-seed random draw of up to 50 works. Where a term set has 50 or fewer works, the sample is the whole set, so the share describes that set. Shares from samples of this size carry wide uncertainty.

The overlap is measured on the sample only. It shows how many sampled works the main plastics query (plastic-v3.1) also retrieves. It is a share of the sample, not a completeness rate for either query.
The probe does not read abstracts. No person has checked the language or topic of any sampled work.
Only the registered strings are searched. A term that is not in the register, a translation or a transliteration is not counted, so these counts are not totals for native-language literature.
not_covered: Lifecycle-and-society and lens terms in any language, for example waste-colonialism, justice and transboundary-trade terms.

Arabic, Turkish, Indonesian, Hindi, Dutch, Polish and other languages: no term strings are registered for them, so they are not searched as languages. Works in these languages can still match a registered string that is spelled the same (see the caveats).
Italian. The A3 probe gives a count of 85 but no term string, so Italian was not run.
